study type: Observational study (comprising longitudinal discovery, longitudinal verification, and case-control phases)
exposure: Circulating RNA transcripts (GMEB2, IGLV1-36, PDCD11, TRBV15, UPF2, CA4, DHRS13, PADI4, SH3BP5, TRAPPC11)
cohort: The study included women with singleton pregnancies undergoing labor induction at term, with preinduction and postinduction peripheral blood sampling.
finding: A panel of 10 circulating birth-associated RNA transcripts were identified, and their preinduction levels were found to be predictive of successful vaginal birth or cesarean delivery after labor induction.
mod_finding: Preinduction levels of GMEB2, IGLV1-36, PDCD11, and UPF2 were most predictive for cesarean birth, with their combined accuracy superior to Bishop score.
